For the broader city, the economic impact of hosting an event of this scale is expected to ripple through hotels, restaurants and local businesses in the days surrounding the race. Whether the Freedom 250 Grand Prix becomes a lasting fixture of the American motorsport calendar or remains a singular chapter tied to the nation's 250th birthday, the sight of open-wheel race cars screaming past the Capitol dome at 180 miles per hour will likely remain one of the most talked-about images of the entire anniversary year.

title: Anthropic Is Gearing Up For An IPO That Could Beat SpaceX's All-Time Record
excerpt: The Claude maker is preparing to file publicly for a mega IPO as soon as the end of August, with bankers and investors now discussing a size that could match or surpass SpaceX's record-breaking $86 billion debut.
body: Anthropic is preparing for a stock market debut that people close to the deal say could rival or top the biggest IPO in history. According to Bloomberg, the Claude developer expects to match or exceed the size of SpaceX's record-setting offering, and could publicly file its paperwork as soon as the end of August.

SpaceX initially targeted $75 billion when it went public earlier this year and ultimately raised $86.2 billion once its overallotment option was exercised. Anthropic executives, led by Chief Financial Officer Krishna Rao, have been briefing investors in recent weeks but have so far declined to confirm a specific valuation target.
From Confidential Filing To Wall Street Debut

Anthropic first submitted a confidential draft registration statement to the Securities and Exchange Commission back on June 1, edging ahead of rival OpenAI in the race to public markets by about a week. Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan are leading the offering, with additional banks reportedly being added to the roster as the deal takes shape.

The company's growth has been staggering by any normal IPO standard. Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate crossed $65 billion by the end of July, up more than sevenfold from where it stood at the end of last year, following a $65 billion Series H round in May that valued the five-year-old company at $965 billion. Some investors briefed on the matter have told the Financial Times they expect annualized revenue to reach $100 billion to $120 billion by year's end.
Chasing A Trillion-Dollar Debut

Reports differ on just how large the eventual valuation could go, with some investor estimates cited by the Financial Times putting a potential figure as high as $2 trillion when the listing arrives, tentatively expected around October. Even more conservative estimates place Anthropic comfortably above the $1 trillion mark, in the same territory analysts expect for OpenAI's own eventual listing.

If the IPO proceeds at anywhere near the scale being discussed, it would help push 2026 past the current record for US IPO volume, a mark of $195.2 billion set in 2021. As of mid-August, this year's total already stood at $160.6 billion, before accounting for Anthropic's potential debut.
Not Without Friction

The run-up to the IPO hasn't been entirely smooth. Anthropic remains in active litigation with the US Department of Defense after being designated a supply-chain risk earlier this year, and the company continues to compete against both OpenAI and a wave of lower-cost open-source alternatives, including options from Chinese developers. Details of the IPO, including its final size and timing, remain subject to change as discussions with investors continue.

title: Nevada Just Approved 8,000 Robotaxis For Tesla, Uber And Waymo To Flood Las Vegas
excerpt: Regulators unanimously cleared permits letting Tesla, Uber and Waymo deploy thousands of driverless vehicles across Clark County over the next year, in what could become the largest robotaxi rollout attempted anywhere in the US.
body: The Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approved permits Thursday that could put as many as 8,000 robotaxis on the streets of Clark County, home to Las Vegas, over the next 12 months. The decision marks the biggest regulatory green light the autonomous vehicle industry has received anywhere in the country to date.

Tesla received by far the largest allocation, with permission to deploy up to 5,000 driverless vehicles, replacing the tiny 10-car interim limit regulators had imposed on the company just weeks earlier. Waymo and Uber were each cleared for up to 1,000 robotaxis, with Uber running its fleet through partnerships with Hyundai subsidiary Motional and Amazon-owned Zoox, which separately holds its own permit for 100 vehicles already operating on the Strip.
From 10 Cars To 5,000

Tesla's turnaround was especially dramatic. The company's original interim permit, issued in late July, capped it at just 10 vehicles confined to a narrow stretch of the Strip, with a 45 mph speed limit and no pickups allowed at Harry Reid International Airport. Thursday's vote replaced that restriction entirely, though Tesla itself downplayed expectations of hitting the full number anytime soon.

"The 5,000 has always been a ceiling for us," Tesla Cybercab chief engineer Eric Early told regulators at the hearing, adding that reaching somewhere around 2,500 vehicles within the next year would already be a strong outcome. Tesla has said broader scaling depends on its next-generation FSD v15 software, expected to ship in late 2026 or early 2027.
A Battleground In The Making

Even a partial rollout would make Clark County one of the most competitive robotaxi markets in the country, with three major players vying for the same riders. Supporters argue the shift could create new categories of jobs tied to maintaining, charging and cleaning driverless fleets, while critics, including the Livery Operators Association, warned the approvals risk oversaturating the local transportation market and displacing human taxi and gig drivers.

Attorney Kimberly Maxson-Rushton, representing the association, raised concerns during the hearing about both market saturation and increased congestion, particularly around the so-called Golden Triangle area that has already seen heavy autonomous vehicle testing. Uber has pushed for a mixed approach that keeps human drivers alongside robotaxis rather than flooding the market all at once.
What Happens Next

Whether any of the three companies can actually hit their approved numbers remains an open question, with even Tesla's own engineers expressing skepticism about reaching their full allocation. Still, the scale of the approval signals that Nevada regulators are betting big on autonomous vehicles reshaping how Las Vegas moves, with the rest of the country now watching closely to see whether the experiment succeeds or exposes the gap between the technology's promise and its real-world readiness.

title: Trump Administration Declares 'Economic Warfare' On Iran As Ceasefire Window Closes For Good
excerpt: With the 60-day US-Iran memorandum expired and no deal reached, Vice President JD Vance says the war has entered a 'new phase' of economic pressure, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent promises the largest coordinated economic isolation campaign in history.
body: The Trump administration is shifting its approach to the war with Iran from battlefield pressure to an all-out economic squeeze, officials signaled this week, after the 60-day window for a lasting US-Iran peace deal expired without an agreement.

Vice President JD Vance said the conflict has entered a "new phase" focused on economic pressure rather than further military escalation. "We're going to keep that going because we think that's the best way to ultimately accomplish the final objective here," Vance said, without detailing specific new measures.
"The Greatest Coordinated Economic Isolation In History"

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent went further in comments to CNBC, describing the coming campaign as "the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world," though he said full details would not be released until Monday. When asked whether the US would also pressure China over its dealings with Iran, Bessent was noncommittal in public, saying "many conversations are best to have in private," while calling on Beijing to "get with the program."
China's foreign ministry pushed back on the framing, with spokesman Lin Jian telling reporters the country would continue to act in line with its own interests rather than external pressure.
A Deadline That Passed Without A Deal

The memorandum of understanding, signed in June at the G7 summit, had given the US and Iran 60 days to negotiate a permanent settlement covering sanctions relief, Iran's nuclear program and the future of the Strait of Hormuz. That window closed earlier this week with no extension announced and no agreement on the table, prompting Iran's Foreign Ministry to say Tehran would shift to a "fully offensive" military posture in response to what it called repeated US violations of the agreement's terms.
A Region Still Under Strain

The economic escalation comes against a backdrop of continued instability across the wider region. Yemen's Houthi movement claimed another attack on a Saudi-linked vessel in the Red Sea this week, a Russian oil tanker ran aground near Oman and began spilling crude onto local beaches, and the United Nations has warned of an "alarming" surge in violence as Israel intensifies operations in Lebanon.

For now, Washington's message is that further military escalation is being replaced, at least for the moment, by financial pressure aimed at squeezing Tehran's economy into returning to the negotiating table — though with full details of the plan still pending, how sharply that pressure will actually bite remains to be seen.

title: IndyCars Are About To Race Past The Capitol For The First Time Ever In DC's Freedom 250 Grand Prix
excerpt: More than 200,000 people are expected on the National Mall this weekend as open-wheel cars hit nearly 200 mph past the Washington Monument in the first-ever motor race held in the nation's capital.
body: For the first time in its history, Washington, D.C. is about to host a car race. The Freedom 250 Grand Prix, a two-day NTT IndyCar Series event, takes over a temporary street circuit around the National Mall on August 22 and 23, with race cars expected to hit speeds close to 200 mph just blocks from the US Capitol.

Organizers say more than 200,000 people are expected to attend across the weekend, making it one of the largest single spectator events D.C. has hosted in years. The race is free to the general public, though the window to request general admission tickets has already closed, and a premium hospitality option, the Champions Club, is available for close to $5,500 per person for the weekend.
A Course Through American History

The 1.7-mile, seven-turn circuit winds past some of the country's most recognizable landmarks, including the Washington Monument, the Capitol's west façade, the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, the National Gallery of Art and the National Archives. Its longest straightaway runs nearly half a mile down Pennsylvania Avenue, a stretch normally capped at 25 mph that drivers will take at speeds approaching 200 mph during the race itself.

Sunday's main event covers 147 laps for a total of roughly 250 miles, honoring the country's 250th anniversary. Saturday features exhibition races featuring NASCAR and IndyCar legends including Jeff Gordon, Kurt Busch, Tony Kanaan and Helio Castroneves, competing in vintage IROC-spec Pontiac Firebirds.
How It Came Together

The race traces back to a January executive order signed by President Trump, directing the Departments of Transportation and the Interior to design a race route through the National Mall as part of the broader America250 semiquincentennial celebrations, which have already included a UFC card on the White House lawn and a nationwide fireworks show. Motorsports company Penske is organizing and funding the event, with any profits reportedly going to local charities.

Organizers have described it as a one-time event tied specifically to the anniversary rather than the start of an annual D.C. fixture. "This is a one-time-only event, because we're celebrating the country's 250th one time," event chair and Penske Corp. president Bud Denker said.
What To Expect On Race Day

The buildout has already reshaped downtown D.C. for the week, with road closures, Metrobus detours and restricted access to some museums near the Mall. The FAA has said it will pause flights at nearby Reagan National Airport for three hours during Sunday's race. For anyone not attending in person, the race will air live nationally on FOX starting at 1 p.m. on Sunday, August 23.

title: UAE Suspends All Trade And Financial Ties With Iran After Accusing Tehran Of Missile Attack
excerpt: Abu Dhabi says it detected two Iranian ballistic missiles aimed at shipping lanes, one landing inside its territorial waters, and has halted all trade and financial dealings with Iran until further notice.
body: The United Arab Emirates has cut off all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran, a dramatic escalation announced Wednesday after Abu Dhabi accused Tehran of firing ballistic missiles toward shipping lanes in the Gulf. It marks the sharpest economic break yet between the two countries since the US-Israel war on Iran began in late February.

The UAE's Defense Ministry said its air defense systems detected two Iranian ballistic missiles overnight, with one landing outside the country's territorial waters and the second falling within them. Officials later said their assessment pointed to the missiles being aimed at maritime navigation rather than at UAE territory directly, which eased fears of a deliberate strike on the mainland even as it underlined how exposed shipping remains near the Strait of Hormuz.
"Until Further Notice"

Announcing the suspension, Foreign Ministry strategic communications director Afra Al Hameli said the halt covered all trade activity, commercial exchange and financial transactions with Tehran, citing regional escalations that undermine peace and security. She also pushed back on unspecified claims about the state of the UAE's economic relationship with Iran, without saying which allegations she meant, while insisting the country remained committed to dialogue and regional integration as the path to stability.

The move follows weeks of accusations from Abu Dhabi that Iran has been targeting its state-owned ADNOC tankers while they transit the strait, and comes after a period of relative calm for the UAE, which had not faced missiles aimed at it since May after bearing the brunt of early attacks in the war. The decision was also reportedly preceded by a phone call between UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan and President Trump.
Iran Denies Involvement

Iran has pushed back hard on the accusation, with reports indicating Tehran is calling the missile incident a false-flag operation rather than an attack it carried out. The denial adds another layer of uncertainty to an already murky picture around the Strait of Hormuz, where multiple parties have traded blame over vessel strikes for months without independent verification of who fired what.

The economic rupture lands just a day after the 60-day window for a broader US-Iran peace deal expired without an agreement, and after President Trump threatened to bomb Oman if it interfered with Washington's push to reopen the strait. Iran's armed forces chief has separately renewed warnings to other Gulf states against assisting the US military, framing any support as effectively joining the war against Tehran, a signal that the diplomatic path out of the conflict may be narrowing further rather than widening.

title: Moderna Shares Nearly Double As Its mRNA Cancer Vaccine With Merck Clears Landmark Trial
excerpt: A personalized mRNA vaccine combined with Merck's Keytruda slowed melanoma recurrence in a large late-stage trial, the first successful Phase 3 result ever recorded for an mRNA cancer therapy.
body: Moderna shares surged as much as 90 percent in premarket trading Wednesday after the company and Merck announced that their personalized mRNA cancer vaccine had succeeded in a major late-stage trial for melanoma, a result researchers are calling a milestone for cancer treatment. Merck's stock climbed more than 8 percent on the same news.

The Phase 3 trial, known as INTerpath-001, enrolled 1,137 patients with high-risk, surgically removed melanoma. Participants either received the experimental vaccine, called intismeran autogene, alongside Merck's immunotherapy Keytruda, or Keytruda by itself for about a year. The combination met its main goal of significantly extending the time patients lived without their cancer returning, and also hit a key secondary target of slowing the disease's spread to other parts of the body.
A First For The Field

Researchers have chased the promise of so-called neoantigen vaccines, shots built from the specific mutations found in a patient's own tumor, for years. This is the first randomized Phase 3 trial to definitively demonstrate that kind of personalized approach can work, and the first positive late-stage result for any mRNA-based cancer treatment. Jedd Wolchok, director of the Meyer Cancer Center at Weill Cornell Medicine, called it proof that something once dismissed as science fiction can now delay the progression of a deadly cancer.

Each dose of the vaccine is manufactured individually. Scientists sequence a patient's tumor after surgery, identify its unique mutations, and build a shot designed to train the immune system to recognize and attack any cancer cells that share those same mutations. Moderna and Merck said no new safety concerns emerged in the trial, with side effects similar to those seen with other common vaccines.
What It Means For Both Companies

For Moderna, the results are a badly needed catalyst. The company has leaned almost entirely on its COVID-19 vaccine for revenue since the pandemic eased, and Wednesday's stock move reflects how much investors have been waiting for a credible path to diversification. Analysts at William Blair upgraded the stock following the announcement, while Barclays had previously estimated the therapy could generate roughly $3 billion a year in melanoma treatment alone by 2035.

For Merck, the timing matters just as much. Keytruda remains the pharmaceutical industry's best-selling drug, bringing in over $32 billion last year, but it faces patent expiration in the coming years. A successful combination therapy gives Merck a plausible way to extend Keytruda's commercial life well beyond that cliff. Both companies say they plan to present full trial data at an upcoming medical conference and begin discussions with regulators, with an estimated 112,000 new melanoma cases and more than 8,500 deaths expected in the US alone this year.

title: Inside The Tupac Shakur Murder Trial, Nearly 30 Years After The Rapper's Killing
excerpt: Witness testimony is underway in Las Vegas in the murder trial of Duane 'Keffe D' Davis, the first and only person ever charged in the 1996 drive-by shooting that killed hip-hop icon Tupac Shakur.
body: Nearly three decades after Tupac Shakur was gunned down on the Las Vegas Strip, the man prosecutors say orchestrated his killing is finally standing trial. Duane "Keffe D" Davis, 63, faces a charge of murder with a deadly weapon with intent to promote a criminal gang, and could spend the rest of his life in prison if convicted.

Opening statements began Monday in a Clark County courtroom packed with Shakur's relatives, reporters and jurors preparing for weeks of testimony. Chief Deputy District Attorney Binu Palal told jurors that while few people connected to the case have ever been willing to talk, Davis has spent decades struggling to stay quiet about his role in it.
An Act Of Revenge, Prosecutors Say

Prosecutors allege the September 7, 1996 drive-by shooting was retaliation for a beating earlier that same night, when Shakur and his entourage attacked Davis's nephew, Orlando Anderson, in the MGM Grand following a Mike Tyson fight. According to the state, Davis did not fire the fatal shots himself but planned and directed the attack that followed hours later, when gunfire from a white Cadillac struck Shakur's vehicle at a nearby intersection.

The defense has pushed back hard, with attorney Michael Sanft telling jurors in his opening statement that the prosecution's case amounts to fiction rather than fact, and arguing that investigators' work over the decades has been inconsistent and incomplete. Sanft has also suggested that no one may ever conclusively solve a case this old, calling the evidence stale after thirty years.
Davis's Own Words Take Center Stage

Much of the state's case rests on Davis's own public statements. He discussed his presence in the car that night with federal investigators in 1998 and 1999, spoke further with Las Vegas police in a 2009 proffer interview, and later detailed his account in a 2019 memoir, Compton Street Legend, in which he described himself as one of the last living eyewitnesses to the shooting. Those recorded admissions, which the defense fought unsuccessfully to keep out of the trial, are expected to feature heavily as testimony continues.

Early witnesses have included retired law enforcement officers who worked the case and a forensic pathologist who walked jurors through Shakur's cause of death, testimony some family members chose to step out of the courtroom for. No one was charged in the killing for 27 years until Davis's 2023 indictment, a gap that turned one of hip-hop's most famous unsolved mysteries into a trial the genre's fans have waited a generation to see.

title: Mattel Honors Marilyn Monroe's 100th Birthday With A New Barbie Inspired By Her Most Iconic Scene
excerpt: The Barbie Signature Marilyn Monroe doll recreates the hot-pink gown from 'Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend,' marking the seventh Barbie modeled on the Hollywood icon and capping a year of centennial tributes.
body: Marilyn Monroe's centennial year has one more tribute to add to the list. Mattel released a new Barbie Signature doll Tuesday inspired by one of the most recognizable scenes in Hollywood history: Monroe's performance of "Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend" in the 1953 musical comedy Gentlemen Prefer Blondes.

The $81 collectible recreates the look in detail, from the strapless hot-pink satin gown and oversized bow to the elbow-length opera gloves and layers of sparkling jewelry Monroe wore while performing the number, which the American Film Institute has ranked among the 12th best film songs of the 20th century. It went on sale August 18 at major US retailers, a little more than two months after what would have been Monroe's 100th birthday on June 1.
Built With The Estate's Involvement

Mattel doll designers Robert Best and Linda Kyaw worked directly with the Estate of Marilyn Monroe LLC throughout the design process to capture both her likeness and the fine details of the on-screen costume. Best said the goal went beyond celebrating Monroe's fashion and film legacy, framing the doll as a nod to her often-overlooked business instincts, since she became one of the first women in Hollywood to found her own production company, Marilyn Monroe Productions, back in 1955.

This marks the seventh Barbie doll modeled on Monroe since Mattel's first attempt in 1997, when the company released a similar pink satin gown look as part of its Hollywood Legends Collection. Other past releases have recreated her billowing white dress from The Seven Year Itch, a red sequined gown from Gentlemen Prefer Blondes, and the one-shouldered evening look from How to Marry a Millionaire.
A Year Of Centennial Tributes

The doll caps a year of celebrations marking Monroe's 100th birthday, including an ongoing exhibition at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles running through February 2027, and a gathering in Palm Springs earlier this year where more than a thousand fans dressed in her iconic white halter dress from The Seven Year Itch, setting a new Guinness World Record while raising money for LGBTQ+ charities.

It's also the second celebrity-inspired Barbie Mattel has released this month alone, following a Whitney Houston doll modeled on her "I Wanna Dance With Somebody" music video look that launched August 8. The pace reflects how central the Barbie Signature line, which has previously honored figures from Shania Twain to Queen Elizabeth II, has become to how Mattel marks major cultural anniversaries.

title: US-Iran Ceasefire Deadline Passes As Trump Threatens To Bomb Oman, Another Tanker Hit In Hormuz
excerpt: The 60-day window for a lasting US-Iran peace deal has expired with no agreement in place, and President Trump is threatening Oman even as a fresh projectile strike hits a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.
body: The 60-day negotiating window the United States and Iran set for themselves in June has come and gone without a lasting peace deal, and the war that has gripped the Middle East since late February shows little sign of winding down. President Donald Trump marked the deadline not with a fresh ultimatum for Tehran, but with a threat directed at one of the region's most consistent mediators: Oman.

Speaking to Fox News on Monday, Trump said the US would respond forcefully if Oman got in the way of Washington's push to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz, using an expletive for emphasis. It was the second time this year he has aimed that kind of threat at Muscat, which has spent weeks negotiating directly with Iran over a mechanism to manage shipping through the waterway even as US-Iran talks have stalled.
A Deadline That Passed Quietly

The memorandum of understanding, signed in June at the G7 summit in France, gave the two sides up to 60 days to hammer out a permanent settlement covering sanctions relief, Iran's nuclear program and the future of the strait, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil once flowed before the war. That window closed Monday with no announced extension and no deal on the table.

Trump insisted he was in no rush, telling reporters he has no fixed timetable and that Iranian officials are quietly negotiating through a backchannel with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, a claim the IRGC has denied. He also renewed his call for Tehran to surrender outright, while Iran's foreign ministry maintained that its talks with Oman over the strait were progressing in good faith.
Another Vessel Struck Off Oman

The diplomatic standoff played out against a fresh escalation at sea. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre reported that a vessel transiting the strait was struck by an unidentified projectile, sustaining engine room damage and at least one crew casualty. It is the latest in a long string of attacks on commercial shipping since the conflict began, with maritime intelligence firms tracking dozens of tankers hit, boarded or forced to reverse course over the past several months.

Traffic through Hormuz has picked up only marginally since the June memorandum, with shippers still routing many vessels around Oman's coastline to avoid the narrowest, most exposed stretch of the strait. Brent crude has ticked up modestly on the renewed uncertainty, trading near $89 a barrel, still well below the peaks seen earlier in the war but a reminder of how tightly global energy markets remain tied to the outcome here.
A Region Still On Edge

The stalled talks come as the wider conflict shows signs of spreading rather than cooling. Houthi forces in Yemen say they struck a Saudi military vessel and its escorts in the Red Sea over the weekend, and Iran's army chief has publicly floated bounties for the capture or killing of American troops in the region. Trump's envoy, Jared Kushner, has meanwhile been shuttling between separate talks aimed at steadying the Gaza ceasefire, underscoring how many fronts the administration is now trying to manage at once.

For now, the strait remains the most closely watched flashpoint. Oman continues to position itself as the go-between it has been for decades, even as it finds itself, once again, in the crosshairs of a US president who has shown he is willing to threaten allies as readily as adversaries when a deal proves elusive.

title: Princess Eugenie Finally Reveals Her Baby Daughter's Name, And It's A Tribute To The Late Queen
excerpt: Two weeks after welcoming her third child in Lisbon, Princess Eugenie has shared her daughter's full name, a nod to Queen Elizabeth II and to the family's ties to Portugal.
body: Princess Eugenie has ended two weeks of speculation over her newborn daughter's name, revealing on Instagram that the baby is called Adelaide Elizabeth Annina Brooksbank. The announcement came exactly a fortnight after the birth, following the same pattern Eugenie set with her first child, whose name she also waited days to share.

Eugenie and her husband, Jack Brooksbank, welcomed Adelaide on August 3 at a hospital in Lisbon, weighing six pounds nine ounces. Buckingham Palace confirmed the birth at the time with a short statement, but the couple kept the name private while they settled into life with a newborn and her two older brothers, five-year-old August and three-year-old Ernest.
A Name Rooted In Two Countries

In her post, Eugenie explained that Adelaide was named after three people the couple loves and admires, including her late great-grandmother, whom the family holds close. She added that the name reflects both English and Portuguese history, the two places she and Brooksbank consider home, since the family splits much of its time between London and Lisbon.

The middle name Elizabeth is the most obvious tribute, echoing the same instinct that has run through several recent royal births, from Princess Charlotte to Prince Harry and Meghan's daughter Lilibet. It continues a pattern in which Eugenie's own children carry names honoring past generations of the family: her elder son's middle name nods to the late Prince Philip, while her second son was named partly after his own grandfathers.
A Princess, But Not A Princess Herself

Adelaide is now 15th in line to the British throne, one place behind her brothers. Because Eugenie's father lost his prince title, and titles in the family have historically passed only through the male line, Adelaide will be styled as "Miss" rather than inheriting any royal title of her own, the same rule that applies to her brothers as "Master."

The photos accompanying the announcement showed Adelaide wrapped in a blanket, cradled by her family and held by her two brothers in what appears to be their first group portrait together. Eugenie, 36, is the younger daughter of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and Sarah Ferguson and a niece of King Charles III, though she and Brooksbank are not working royals and largely keep their family life out of official palace duties.

title: Magnus Carlsen Goes Unbeaten Again To Defend His Esports World Cup Chess Crown In Paris
excerpt: The Norwegian grandmaster swept Denis Lazavik in the Grand Final without dropping a single game across the whole tournament, cementing his status as the sport's most dominant player of the rapid era.
body: Magnus Carlsen has done it again. A year after winning the inaugural chess event at the Esports World Cup, the Norwegian grandmaster successfully defended his title in Paris on Saturday, beating 19-year-old Belarusian challenger Denis Lazavik in straight sets in the Grand Final without losing a single game across the entire competition.

Carlsen finished the tournament with 11 wins and nine draws, an accuracy rate CNN reported at 99.2 percent, on his way to a $250,000 first-place prize and 1,000 crucial points for his club, Team Liquid, in the event's broader Club Championship standings. It extends a run in which he has never lost a match at the Esports World Cup since the chess event was introduced.
A Dominant, If Understated, Run

The 35-year-old entered the $1.5 million tournament as the heavy favorite, unsurprising given he has held the world number one ranking for a staggering 15 consecutive years, the longest such streak in modern FIDE history. Despite that pedigree, Carlsen played down expectations heading into the event, telling CNN Sports he tries not to think too much about winning and instead focuses on taking each game step by step.

That approach carried him through a stacked 22-player field that included Hikaru Nakamura, Alireza Firouzja, Ian Nepomniachtchi and India's Arjun Erigaisi. Lazavik, representing the AG.AL organization, reached the final on the strength of a playoff run in which he eliminated Nakamura in the semifinals, and he managed to draw four games against Carlsen in the final. He simply couldn't find a way to win one.
Speed Chess Suits Him

The tournament was played at a rapid 10-minute time control with no increment, a fast-paced format that rewards the kind of intuitive, practical decision-making Carlsen has built his reputation on rather than long calculation. Woman Grandmaster and event commentator Nemo Zhou put it bluntly to CNN Sports, calling Carlsen the greatest of all time without hesitation.

Carlsen, who is also a five-time classical world champion and the reigning FIDE Freestyle Chess World Champion, voluntarily gave up his classical title in 2023, saying he no longer felt motivated to defend it. Rapid and freestyle formats, by contrast, have kept pulling him back into competition, and results like this weekend's suggest retirement from the top of the game remains a long way off.

According to Chess.com, last year's Esports World Cup chess event drew close to 260,000 peak concurrent viewers, more than traditional fixtures like Norway Chess and the Tata Steel tournament, a sign of how much audience the faster, higher-stakes format has been able to pull in for a game more often associated with quiet, hours-long contemplation.

title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT For Teens With Stricter Guardrails As Lawsuits Over Child Safety Mount
excerpt: The $852 billion startup is rolling out a dedicated teen experience with study tools, parental controls and tighter content limits, as it faces lawsuits alleging its chatbot contributed to harm involving minors.
body: OpenAI began rolling out ChatGPT for Teens on Tuesday, a dedicated version of its chatbot for users aged 13 to 17 that adds stronger content restrictions, homework-focused tools and new controls for parents. The rollout starts globally for eligible Free and paid personal accounts, with full availability in Australia expected by early September.

Any account that identifies itself as belonging to a 13-to-17-year-old, or that OpenAI's age-prediction system estimates likely belongs to someone under 18, will be automatically switched into the teen experience. Users don't need to do anything to activate it, and OpenAI says that when it isn't confident about someone's age, it will default to the safer, more restricted version rather than the standard adult experience.
Learning Over Shortcuts

A central pitch of the new product is steering teenagers toward actually learning material rather than letting the chatbot simply produce finished homework. A built-in Study Mode walks users through problems with guiding questions and step-by-step support, and the system is designed to detect when a teen appears to be trying to shortcut an assignment, redirecting them back into that guided format. Parents or teens can also set dedicated Study Hours during which the mode switches on automatically.

On the safety side, OpenAI says the teen version will refuse romantic or flirtatious language and will be more firmly instructed never to imply it has feelings or consciousness of its own, changes the company frames as an effort to cut down on unhealthy emotional attachment to the chatbot. Teen accounts will also see more frequent reminders to take breaks during long sessions and extra warnings before uploading images that could be private or sensitive.
Parents Get More Levers

Parents who link their account to a teen's, something both parties have to agree to, can now set quiet hours that block access to ChatGPT entirely, manage settings like memory and chat history, and receive alerts in a narrow set of high-risk situations, including when the system detects possible self-harm risk or, newly, certain eating-disorder-related warning signs. Even without parental controls turned on, OpenAI says the baseline teen protections apply automatically.
A Launch Under Pressure

The rollout lands at a sensitive moment for the company. OpenAI, now valued at roughly $852 billion and reportedly preparing for what could be one of the largest IPOs in history, is fighting multiple lawsuits alleging that conversations with ChatGPT contributed to the deaths of teenage users, including a widely covered case involving a 16-year-old in California. Child-safety researchers have separately documented instances of the chatbot giving minors troublingly specific guidance on risky behavior when prompted persistently enough.

OpenAI's VP of global policy, Ann O'Leary, said the goal was to treat teens like teens rather than talking down to them or exposing them to material they shouldn't see, while acknowledging that no set of guardrails is completely unbeatable. The company has framed the launch as one piece of a broader effort that began with parental controls last year and will keep expanding as its age-prediction technology matures.

title: Nigel Farage Wins The Byelection He Triggered Himself, Beats A Man Dressed As A Trash Can
excerpt: Nigel Farage is back in the UK Parliament after comfortably winning a special election he called himself, with Britain's mainstream parties sitting the race out and his closest challenger being a costumed novelty candidate.
body: Nigel Farage is once again a Member of Parliament, just over a month after he voluntarily gave up the job. The Reform UK leader comfortably won a byelection in his Essex constituency of Clacton on Thursday, a contest he triggered himself and one that none of Britain's major political parties bothered to contest.

Farage resigned from Parliament on July 7, saying he wanted to seek a fresh mandate from voters. The move came as a parliamentary standards commissioner was investigating whether he had failed to properly declare a roughly £5 million ($6.7 million) gift he received from an overseas crypto investor before he was elected in 2024. Farage has maintained he did nothing wrong, arguing the money was a personal gift intended to help cover his security costs and that he was under no legal obligation to disclose it.
An Election With No Real Opposition

What made the byelection unusual wasn't the result so much as the field of candidates. Labour, the Conservatives, and the other established parties all declined to field candidates, dismissing the vote as a stunt engineered by Farage to draw attention away from the ongoing investigation into his finances. That left Farage facing a lineup of largely fringe and novelty candidates, more than 30 in total.

His most prominent rival ended up being Count Binface, a self-described "intergalactic space warrior" played by comedian Jon Harvey, who has built a long-running career out of running for office against sitting prime ministers and other high-profile politicians. Despite having no realistic path to winning, Binface put in a respectable showing, finishing second with roughly 9,455 votes to Farage's 22,239.
A Bigger Win Than His Original Election

Farage's vote count actually came in about 1,000 higher than what he received when he first won the seat in the 2024 general election, giving him grounds to frame the result as a personal endorsement rather than a mere formality. Turnout was higher than many expected too, with roughly 44 percent of eligible voters in the constituency casting a ballot despite the contest falling in the middle of the summer holiday season and on one of the hottest days of the year.

Speaking to supporters after the result was announced, Farage described the win as proof that voters in Clacton had rejected what he called the political establishment's attempt to sideline him. He did not attend the official overnight vote count in person, citing security advice from local police, choosing instead to celebrate with supporters at a separate event.
The Investigation Isn't Over

While the election victory secures Farage's return to the House of Commons, it doesn't make his legal troubles disappear. The parliamentary standards investigation into the undisclosed donation, which had been paused when he stepped down, resumed within hours of the result being confirmed. That means Farage returns to Parliament with the same cloud hanging over him that prompted his resignation in the first place, only now with a fresh electoral mandate to point to if the pressure builds further.
Why It Matters Beyond Clacton

Farage has long been one of the most consequential figures in modern British politics, having played a central role in the campaign for Britain to leave the European Union and, more recently, in building Reform UK into a party some pollsters now see as a genuine contender for power. His byelection strategy, essentially daring his opponents not to show up and then claiming vindication when they don't, is a tactic that could resurface again if his finances continue to draw scrutiny.

For now, though, Farage returns to Westminster with a larger vote share, a fresh talking point about establishment parties refusing to face him at the ballot box, and an unresolved investigation still working its way through Parliament's standards process. Whether the episode ends up strengthening his political standing or simply delaying a harder reckoning with the allegations against him is likely to become clearer in the months ahead.

title: San Francisco Rents Have Overtaken New York, And The AI Boom Is Why
excerpt: San Francisco has quietly become the most expensive rental market in America, with average rents climbing 18 percent in under two years as AI companies flood the city with high-paying jobs and squeeze an already tight housing supply.
body: For years, San Francisco lived in New York City's shadow when it came to bragging rights for the most punishing rental market in the country. That has now changed. According to data from real estate firm CoStar, the average asking rent in San Francisco has climbed roughly 18 percent in under two years, pushing the city past New York to claim the title of most expensive major rental market in the United States.

The driver behind the surge isn't a mystery. It's the same force reshaping large parts of the American economy right now: artificial intelligence. Companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have been expanding rapidly in the Bay Area, hiring aggressively and paying salaries that increasingly resemble Wall Street compensation packages rather than typical tech-industry pay.
Where The Money Is Landing

The rent increases haven't been spread evenly across the city. Neighborhoods closest to major AI offices, particularly SoMa and Mission Bay near OpenAI's headquarters, have seen rents climb well above 10 percent year over year, while more residential parts of the city have moved far less. Nearby Silicon Valley cities with heavy concentrations of tech offices, including Mountain View, Palo Alto and Sunnyvale, are experiencing similarly steep increases.

Analysts have compared the pattern to what New York went through in the 2000s as Wall Street rebuilt itself around hedge funds, where new wealth concentrated tightly around specific zip codes before pulling up prices in the surrounding area. Unlike the last major tech boom, though, this new wave of money isn't spreading out into the suburbs. It's staying put in the city itself, in part because AI companies have been pushing for more in-office and hybrid work rather than fully remote arrangements.
Supply Hasn't Kept Up

On the other side of the equation is a supply problem that has been building for years. San Francisco's apartment vacancy rate has fallen to roughly 3 percent in the most sought-after neighborhoods, down from around 13 percent in 2020, according to real estate tracking firms. New housing construction has slowed to a crawl in the city, meaning even a modest increase in demand from well-paid new residents translates quickly into sharply higher prices.

One senior researcher at CoStar likened the current rental market to a pressure cooker heating up fast, a description that tracks with reports of prospective tenants offering above asking rent, paying several months in advance, and in some cases submitting personal biographies to landlords in an effort to stand out in a crowded field of applicants.
Even Six-Figure Salaries Aren't Enough

Perhaps the most striking part of the story is who's being squeezed. It isn't just entry-level workers or people outside the tech industry struggling to keep up. Reports have highlighted tech employees earning around $200,000 a year who say they are still being priced out of desirable neighborhoods, with some choosing to relocate to outlying areas like Lake Tahoe rather than continue competing for housing in the city.

Some AI startups have responded by offering their own workarounds. A handful of companies now provide monthly rent stipends to employees who choose to live within walking distance of the office, arguing that shorter commutes translate into happier, more productive teams. It's a small-scale fix for a much larger structural problem, but it illustrates just how central housing costs have become to hiring conversations in the AI industry.
A Familiar Story With A New Name

San Francisco has been one of the most expensive cities in America for well over a decade, so the underlying dynamics here aren't entirely new. What's changed is the scale and speed of the latest wave, driven almost entirely by a single industry pouring enormous amounts of capital and talent into a relatively small geographic footprint. With several AI companies still expanding and additional public offerings expected in the sector, there's little indication the pressure on San Francisco's housing market is going to ease anytime soon.

title: Belgium Is Fighting Its Largest Wildfire On Record, And It's Still Not Under Control
excerpt: A wildfire tearing through Belgium's High Fens nature reserve has scorched more than 27 square kilometers, forced hundreds to evacuate, and pulled in emergency crews and aircraft from across the European Union.
body: Firefighters in eastern Belgium are battling the largest wildfire the country has recorded in its modern history, with the blaze having burned through more than 27 square kilometers of protected nature reserve as of Sunday and showing no signs of being fully contained.

The fire broke out on Friday in the High Fens, a vast nature reserve of peatlands and pine forest near the German border, and spread rapidly through the following days as hot, dry conditions fed the flames. By Saturday evening, officials in the Liège province said the fire had already scorched around 2,700 hectares, up sharply from roughly 1,600 hectares earlier the same day.
Hundreds Told To Leave Their Homes

As shifting winds pushed smoke into nearby communities, authorities ordered around 600 residents in the municipalities of Waimes and Bütgenbach to evacuate. Tourists in the area were also advised to leave, and a nearby gymnasium was opened to house people displaced by the fire. Local officials warned that unnecessary traffic in the area could hamper the movement of emergency vehicles and complicate an already difficult firefighting effort.

Liège's provincial governor said more than 250 emergency personnel had been deployed to fight the blaze, including over 100 firefighters from both Belgium and neighboring Germany, alongside police, military units and civil protection staff.
Europe Steps In

Given the scale of the fire, Belgium activated the European Union's civil protection mechanism to bring in outside help. Helicopters and water-bomber aircraft were deployed from Czechia, Sweden and the Netherlands to assist Belgian crews already on the ground, underscoring just how significant the blaze has become relative to the country's usual firefighting capacity.

A spokesperson for the regional authorities in Wallonia said the fire had not yet been brought under control as of the weekend, and cautioned that the terrain itself was making the job harder. Much of the affected area consists of difficult-to-access peatland and dense forest, conditions that limit how directly emergency crews can approach the flames.
The Worst Since 1911

Officials have described the current blaze as Belgium's largest wildfire in modern memory, far surpassing a 2011 fire in the same region that had previously held the record after burning close to 14 square kilometers. Historical accounts point to a comparable fire in 1911, during a similarly extreme period of heat and drought, as the last time this particular landscape saw destruction on this scale.

Officials cited unusually dry soil conditions this year as a key factor in why the fire has spread faster and burned deeper than the historical comparison from 2011, even though both blazes struck the same general area.
Part Of A Wider Pattern

The Belgian fire comes amid a broader run of extreme heat and wildfire activity across Western Europe this summer, with France, England and other parts of the continent also dealing with record temperatures and elevated fire risk in recent weeks. For a country not typically associated with large-scale wildfires, the scale of the High Fens blaze has become a stark example of how climate-driven extremes are increasingly showing up in places that historically haven't had to plan for them.

As of Sunday, firefighters remained focused on containment rather than declaring the fire under control, with authorities continuing to monitor wind patterns that could either help crews gain ground or push the blaze toward populated areas nearby.

title: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Is Rewriting The Box Office Record Books
excerpt: Tom Holland's fourth solo outing as Spider-Man has smashed opening-weekend records, crossed a billion dollars faster than almost any film in history, and is now on pace to challenge the highest-grossing movies ever made.
body: It's been a big month for Spider-Man, and an even bigger one for Sony and Marvel Studios. "Spider-Man: Brand New Day," the fourth solo film starring Tom Holland as Peter Parker, has spent the past several weeks demolishing box office records at a pace that has genuinely surprised industry watchers, even ones who expected the film to perform well.

The film opened to a record-breaking $360 million domestically, edging out "Avengers: Endgame" for the biggest opening weekend in North American box office history. It also set the all-time record for domestic preview screenings at $74.5 million, topping Endgame's previous mark, and delivered the highest-grossing Monday ever recorded, beating a longstanding "Black Panther" benchmark.
The Fastest Billion In Years

Global audiences responded just as enthusiastically. "Brand New Day" crossed $1 billion worldwide in only six days, making it the second-fastest film in history to hit that milestone, trailing only "Avengers: Endgame," which reached the same number in five days back in 2019. From there, the film kept climbing, passing $700 million domestically and $1 billion internationally within a matter of weeks, a combination that pushed its worldwide total past $1.6 billion.

That international haul alone was enough to make "Brand New Day" Sony's biggest release ever overseas, surpassing even "Spider-Man: No Way Home," which had held that title since its 2021 release. With its current trajectory, "Brand New Day" is now the 12th highest-grossing film of all time worldwide, and industry analysts believe it has a real shot at joining the small group of films that have crossed $2 billion globally, a club that currently includes just seven movies, among them "Avatar," "Titanic" and "Avengers: Endgame."
Why It's Connecting

Marvel had been coming off a stretch of comparatively underwhelming releases before "Brand New Day" arrived, which made the scale of its success even more notable within the industry. Sony's motion pictures chairman pointed to something simpler than superhero spectacle to explain the film's global appeal, framing it as a story fundamentally about friendship and connection that resonates regardless of where audiences are watching it.

Much of the pre-release buzz also centered on the real-life star power of its two leads. Tom Holland and Zendaya, who are married, generated what analytics firm RelishMix described as a record combined social media following heading into the film's release, spanning platforms like TikTok, YouTube and Instagram. Industry marketers have credited that off-screen chemistry, paired with the pair's relatively private personal lives, with fueling intense fan curiosity that translated directly into ticket sales.
Part Of A Historic Summer

"Brand New Day" isn't carrying the summer alone. It arrived alongside Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey," which has also performed strongly and became the highest-grossing film of Nolan's career after crossing $1.1 billion globally. Together, the two films have helped push the 2026 summer box office toward $4 billion domestically, a benchmark Hollywood hasn't consistently hit since before the pandemic reshaped moviegoing habits.

Including other 2026 hits like "The Super Mario Galaxy Movie," "Michael," and "Toy Story 5," this year has already produced more billion-dollar films than any year since 2019, when nine movies crossed that threshold. Industry estimates now suggest total domestic box office revenue for 2026 could top $10 billion for the first time since then, buoyed further by upcoming late-year releases like "Dune: Part Three" and "Avengers: Doomsday."
What Comes Next

With minimal major competition left on the summer release calendar, "Brand New Day" is expected to keep adding to its totals well into the fall, driven by repeat viewings from longtime fans and steady word-of-mouth. Whether it ultimately catches "No Way Home's" full run of $1.9 billion or pushes into the $2 billion range remains to be seen, but its opening weeks alone have already secured its place among the biggest theatrical releases in recent memory.

title: Spotify Will Start Labeling AI-Generated Artists With a New 'AI Persona' Badge
excerpt: Starting in mid-September, Spotify will flag artist profiles that represent AI-generated identities and exclude them from algorithmic recommendations by default, in one of the music industry's most direct moves yet against synthetic artists.
body: Spotify announced this week that it will begin labeling artist profiles with a new "AI Persona" badge starting in mid-September, targeting cases where an artist's public identity — rather than necessarily the music itself — appears to be entirely AI-generated. The badge will show up on the artist's profile page, in relevant search results, and within playlist track listings, giving listeners a clear signal when they're following an act that isn't actually a real person.

Crucially, Spotify says the distinction is about identity, not production process. An artist who uses AI tools somewhere in their songwriting or production workflow won't automatically be flagged; the badge is reserved specifically for profiles where the artist's name and imagery represent a photorealistic AI-generated persona rather than a real human being building a career in music.
How It Will Work

Spotify says it won't rely solely on artists disclosing their own AI status, though the platform will let artists voluntarily identify as AI Personas through Spotify for Artists. The company will also actively review profiles itself, using detection methods to flag cases it believes represent synthetic identities. Artists who are flagged will be notified and given a chance to appeal if they believe the label was applied incorrectly.

Perhaps the most consequential part of the announcement is that AI Persona profiles will be excluded from Spotify's editorial and algorithmic recommendations by default, meaning they won't appear in playlists like Discover Weekly or Release Radar unless a listener has specifically chosen to follow them. Since those recommendation systems are often the primary way independent artists without major label backing reach new listeners, the change effectively narrows AI Personas' path to organic growth while leaving their music fully accessible to anyone who seeks it out directly.
Part of a Bigger Industry Push

The move builds on a broader Artist Identity & Trust initiative Spotify has been rolling out over the past year, including verification badges, AI-generated music detection tools, and protections against unauthorized AI voice clones and deepfakes. It also arrives shortly after the EU AI Act's transparency requirements for AI-generated audio became enforceable across all 27 member states on August 2, and about a month after a coalition including the RIAA and IFPI proposed voluntary AI labeling standards for streaming platforms industry-wide.

The policy follows growing listener discomfort with synthetic acts, most notably the controversy around The Velvet Sundown, an AI-generated band that racked up millions of streams last year while posing as a real group, even landing on algorithmic playlists with hundreds of thousands of followers. In its announcement, Spotify said its programming is focused on elevating music from authentic artists building real careers, framing the new badge as a matter of basic transparency rather than a judgment on AI as a creative tool.

title: Europe's First Total Solar Eclipse in Nearly Three Decades Draws Massive Crowds
excerpt: The August 12 total solar eclipse plunged parts of Greenland, Iceland and northern Spain into daytime darkness, marking the first total eclipse over mainland Europe since 1999.
body: Crowds gathered across northern Spain, Iceland and Greenland on August 12 to witness the year's only total solar eclipse, an event that marked the first total eclipse visible from mainland Europe since 1999 and the first seen from continental European Union territory since 1999. The path of totality traced a dramatic route starting over Siberia, arcing across the North Pole, down the eastern coast of Greenland, past western Iceland, and finally across the Atlantic to fade out over northern Spain just before sunset.

Totality lasted less than two minutes for most viewers positioned directly in the Moon's shadow, but the effect was striking wherever it occurred: skies went fully dark in the middle of the day, temperatures noticeably dropped, and in several locations observers reported animals reacting as though night had suddenly fallen. Cities including A Coruña, Valencia, Zaragoza, Palma and Bilbao fell within the path of totality, while both Madrid and Barcelona sat just outside it, leaving those cities with only a deep partial eclipse.
Watched Across Two Continents

While the total eclipse itself was confined to a narrow band, a much wider partial eclipse was visible across a huge swath of the Northern Hemisphere, including all of Europe, North Africa, parts of Asia, and much of North America. In the United States, the partial eclipse was visible primarily in northern and northeastern states, with cities like Boston, Philadelphia, Washington D.C. and Portland catching a modest bite taken out of the Sun in the early afternoon hours.

Because the eclipse occurred just over two days after the Moon reached its closest point to Earth this month, its apparent size was slightly larger than average, intensifying the darkness experienced during totality. NASA and the European Space Agency both released detailed path maps ahead of the event, and safety officials repeatedly urged the public to use certified eclipse glasses meeting the ISO 12312-2 standard for any direct viewing outside the brief window of full totality.
Looking Ahead to the Next One

Total solar eclipses occur roughly every 18 months somewhere on Earth, but any single location typically waits centuries between events. Europe won't have to wait nearly that long for its next one: a total solar eclipse is set to cross Spain, North Africa and the Middle East on August 2, 2027, followed by an annular eclipse visible from South America, Portugal and Spain in January 2028.

For American eclipse chasers, the wait is considerably longer. The next total solar eclipse to touch US soil won't arrive until 2044, and even then it will only be visible from Montana, North Dakota and South Dakota, with a more widely accessible coast-to-coast eclipse not expected again until 2045.

title: Pakistan End Three-Year Overseas Test Drought With Series-Levelling Win Over West Indies
excerpt: Babar Azam's return as Test captain got off to a winning start as Pakistan bounced back from a first-Test defeat to level the series 1-1, powered by centuries from Abdullah Shafique and Babar himself.
body: Pakistan salvaged a share of their two-match Test series against the West Indies, bouncing back from a 90-run defeat in the opening Test in Tarouba to win the second Test in Port of Spain by eight wickets, sealing the series 1-1. The result marked Pakistan's first away Test win in three years, snapping an eight-match losing streak on foreign soil.

Chasing a modest target of 75 in the second innings, Pakistan made light work of the run chase despite losing early wickets to Jayden Seales and a mix-up that saw Azan Awais edge onto his stumps. Babar Azam and Abdullah Shafique, the two batting heroes of Pakistan's first innings, steadied the chase before Babar danced down the wicket to smash Jomel Warrican for successive sixes and seal the win shortly after lunch on the fourth day.
Shafique and Babar Lead the Way

Abdullah Shafique was named Player of the Match after a match haul of 160 not out and 24 not out, anchoring Pakistan's total in the first innings and guiding them home unbeaten in the chase. Babar Azam, playing his second stint as Pakistan's Test captain, finished the series with 193 runs and was named Player of the Series, capping a strong personal comeback with both bat and leadership.

West Indies all-rounder Justin Greaves had an outstanding series of his own, finishing with 111 runs and seven wickets and earning Player of the Series honors for the home side, a reflection of how competitive the two-match series proved despite the lopsided nature of the second Test's finish.
A Familiar Scoreline

The 1-1 result extends a curious pattern between the two sides, marking the third consecutive Test series between Pakistan and West Indies to end in a drawn scoreline. Pakistan's spin attack, led by Sajid Khan and supported by pace bowlers Mohammad Ali and Mohammad Abbas, did much of the heavy lifting across the series, while the tourists made several changes to their bowling combinations as they searched for the right balance overseas.

With the series now behind them, Pakistan will look to carry the momentum into their upcoming tour of England, where they are set to play three Tests between August 19 and September 13 as part of the ongoing World Test Championship cycle. The overseas win in Port of Spain offers a timely confidence boost ahead of what promises to be a much sterner test in English conditions.

title: Oil Prices Stay Volatile as Strait of Hormuz Talks Between the US and Iran Drag On
excerpt: Crude prices have swung wildly for weeks as negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz repeatedly stall, with roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply still bottlenecked by the ongoing standoff.
body: Oil markets remain on edge as negotiations between the United States and Iran over reopening the Strait of Hormuz continue to stall, with Brent crude swinging between roughly $78 and $90 a barrel over the past two weeks alone. The strait, a chokepoint that normally carries about a fifth of the world's oil supply, has seen traffic collapse to a fraction of pre-conflict levels since fighting broke out between the US, Israel and Iran earlier this year.

Ship-tracking data from MarineTraffic showed only eight to fifteen vessels crossing the strait on some recent days, compared with roughly 130 transits before the conflict began. The disruption has been described by analysts as the largest energy supply shock in recorded history, forcing tankers to either wait indefinitely or turn back entirely rather than risk passage through contested waters.
A Deal That Keeps Slipping Away

The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding back on June 17 aimed at reopening Hormuz to commercial shipping, but the agreement collapsed almost immediately as fighting resumed over which specific routes vessels would be allowed to use. Iran has continued to demand that ships sail through its territorial waters when transiting the strait, while the US has maintained a naval blockade in response to renewed attacks on tankers.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent suggested in early August that a breakthrough deal could arrive within days, and President Trump has repeatedly signaled that talks were close to a resolution. But each round of optimism has been followed by setbacks: Iranian state media published a restrictive draft proposal that would ban US and Israeli vessels outright and impose steep penalties on other nations it accuses of wrongdoing, while Iran's foreign ministry has separately demanded that Washington lift its naval blockade and pay war reparations before any deal can proceed.
What It Means for Prices

The back-and-forth has kept traders on edge, with Brent crude still up roughly 16% to 24% compared with levels before the US-Israel war on Iran began in late February. The US Energy Information Administration does not expect Middle East oil production to return to anywhere near pre-conflict levels until early 2027, and projects Brent will average around $87 a barrel for the year.

Analysts warn that further escalation, including any new Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure or a sustained deadlock in talks, could send prices sharply higher again. For now, markets are stuck in a holding pattern, reacting to every fresh headline out of Washington, Tehran and Muscat, where Iran and Oman continue separate negotiations over how shipping through the strait might eventually resume.

title: Record-Breaking Climber Nirmal Purja Killed in Avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak
excerpt: The Nepali mountaineer who once scaled all 14 of the world's highest peaks in record time died alongside nine others when an avalanche swept their expedition off Broad Peak in Pakistan's Karakoram range.
body: World-renowned mountaineer Nirmal "Nims" Purja has died in an avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak, the world's 12th-highest mountain, along with nine other members of his expedition. Purja, 43, and his team were struck while attempting the technically demanding 26,414-foot peak in the Karakoram mountain range in Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan region on July 30.

The avalanche swept the ten climbers down the mountain's main west-facing gulley, in some cases carrying them nearly a vertical mile. A rescue and recovery mission launched immediately, with military helicopters and ground teams from the Alpine Club of Pakistan searching the difficult terrain, but officials confirmed by August 1 that Purja and the rest of the group had not survived.
A Legendary Climbing Career

Purja rose to global fame in 2019 when he became the first person to summit all 14 of the world's mountains above 8,000 meters in just six months and six days, a feat that had previously been expected to take years. His achievement, chronicled in the Netflix documentary 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible, turned the former British special forces soldier into one of the most recognizable figures in mountaineering, known for his charisma as much as his climbing records.

Before turning to elite mountaineering, Purja served with the Nepal-born Gurkhas and later in Britain's Special Boat Service, where regulations prevented him from discussing his deployments in detail, though he said he took part in every theater of conflict Britain was involved in during his service. He founded the Nimsdai Foundation in 2022 to support Nepal's Sherpa community, a group he frequently credited for making high-altitude mountaineering possible.
A Dangerous Recovery Effort

Recovering the bodies has proven extremely difficult given ongoing avalanche risk on the mountain. Pakistani climber Sirbaz Khan, the first Pakistani to summit all 14 eight-thousanders without supplemental oxygen, told reporters that rescue teams were dealing with two or three additional avalanches every day as they worked to locate and retrieve the climbers. Purja's body was eventually located, though as of early August it remained stuck in a dangerous section of the mountain that rescuers had not yet been able to safely reach.

Tributes poured in from across the climbing world and beyond, including from UK Defence Minister Wes Streeting, who said he was deeply saddened by the loss. The Nimsdai Foundation said in a statement that Purja's legacy would live on through the countless people he inspired to pursue their own version of the impossible.

title: Aubrey Plaza Welcomes Her First Baby With Christopher Abbott
excerpt: The Parks and Recreation and White Lotus star is officially a first-time mom, giving birth to a baby girl more than a year after the loss of her husband, Jeff Baena.
body: Aubrey Plaza is officially a mother. The actress welcomed her first child, a baby girl, with partner Christopher Abbott during the last week of July, according to sources close to the couple. Plaza was spotted in New York City on August 9 holding her newborn while attending Abbott's final performance in the Broadway revival of Death of a Salesman, marking the first public sighting of the baby.

The pregnancy first came to light in dramatic fashion back in April, when Plaza casually revealed the news during an appearance on the Smartless podcast, telling hosts Will Arnett, Jason Bateman and Sean Hayes, "There's a baby inside me," while recounting a doctor's visit. A representative for Plaza later confirmed the pregnancy to People, describing it as a beautiful surprise following an emotionally difficult year.
A New Chapter After Loss

The baby's arrival comes roughly 18 months after the death of Plaza's estranged husband, filmmaker Jeff Baena, who died by suicide in January 2025. Plaza and Baena had quietly separated in the months before his death, and the news drew an outpouring of support alongside some public reflection on how quickly her life had changed in the time since.

Plaza and Abbott's relationship grew out of a long professional partnership. The pair first worked together on the 2020 Sundance thriller Black Bear and later reunited for an off-Broadway revival of Danny and the Deep Blue Sea in 2023. They made their red carpet debut as a couple at the 2026 Tony Awards, where Abbott was nominated for his role in Death of a Salesman, before confirming the pregnancy publicly just weeks later.
Keeping It Private

True to form for two famously private actors, Plaza and Abbott have said little publicly about the pregnancy or birth beyond the initial confirmations, and neither has commented directly on the baby's arrival. Plaza did make a point of showing off her baby bump at Paris Fashion Week in March, sitting front row at the Loewe show in an oversized leather jacket, before mostly staying out of the spotlight as her due date approached.

For Plaza, 41, best known for her breakout role as April Ludgate on Parks and Recreation and more recent turns in The White Lotus and Ingrid Goes West, the new arrival marks a deeply personal milestone in a year that has otherwise kept her largely out of the public eye.

title: England Survive 10-Goal Thriller to Beat France 6-4 and Claim World Cup Bronze
excerpt: Bukayo Saka's hat-trick powered England to their best World Cup finish since 1966, in a wild third-place match that saw them blow a four-goal lead before holding on in Miami.
body: England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 with a stunning 6-4 win over France in the tournament's third-place playoff at Miami's Hard Rock Stadium, capping the highest-scoring men's World Cup knockout match since 1954. Bukayo Saka's hat-trick was the headline act, but the game will be remembered as much for England nearly squandering a commanding four-goal cushion as for the individual brilliance on display.

England raced into a 4-0 halftime lead that looked to have the match well in hand. Declan Rice opened the scoring in just the third minute with a curling strike from distance, one of the earliest goals in England's World Cup history, before assisting Ezri Konsa's header from a corner. Saka then struck twice before the break, first tapping in from a Marcus Rashford pass and then finishing sharply from the edge of the box.
France's Second-Half Fightback

France, who had looked disinterested for most of the first half, transformed after the restart. Kylian Mbappé pulled a goal back in the 48th minute before Bradley Barcola made it 4-2, and Mbappé struck again in the 66th to suddenly put France within one goal, sending nerves through the England camp. Saka restored some breathing room with a penalty to complete his hat-trick, but Ousmane Dembélé's late strike in stoppage time made it 5-4 and set up a tense finish.

Jude Bellingham finally settled the match in the eighth minute of stoppage time, dribbling past three French defenders inside the box before slotting home to make it 6-4 and confirm England's bronze medal. Mbappé's brace in the match also made him the World Cup's all-time leading scorer, adding another individual milestone to a night already packed with them.
A Historic Finish for England

The result gives England their best World Cup finish on foreign soil and their highest placing overall since lifting the trophy on home turf in 1966. Saka became only the second England player, after Sir Geoff Hurst, to score a hat-trick in a World Cup knockout match, and just the second player in tournament history to do so against France, joining Brazil's Pelé, who managed the feat in 1958.

Head coach Thomas Tuchel, who had heard boos from sections of England fans before kickoff following a difficult tournament, struck a measured tone in his post-match press conference, noting that the medal was England's first at a World Cup in 60 years even as he acknowledged the semifinal exit to Argentina still stung. With France's Didier Deschamps set to hand the reins to Zinedine Zidane before the 2028 Euros on home soil, both sides now turn toward rebuilding for the next major tournament cycle.

title: Andrew and Tristan Tate Arrested in Miami as UK Pursues Extradition on Dozens of New Charges
excerpt: The controversial influencer brothers were taken into custody by US Marshals after British prosecutors filed dozens of additional charges, testing the limits of their political connections in Washington.
body: Influencer brothers Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested by US Marshals in Miami on July 18 after British prosecutors filed a fresh wave of charges against them, triggering a UK extradition request that is now working its way through US courts. The dual British-American citizens are being held in a Florida prison as they fight to avoid being sent back to the United Kingdom.

The UK's Crown Prosecution Service said the new charges bring the total number of alleged offenses against the brothers to 59, spanning seven victims and covering conduct authorities say occurred between 2010 and 2017 in the East of England region. Andrew Tate faces the larger share of the charges, including counts of rape, trafficking for sexual exploitation, assault, and offenses tied to indecent images of a child. Tristan Tate faces a smaller number of charges covering sexual assault, rape, and trafficking.
A Long-Running Legal Saga

This is far from the Tates' first brush with the law. The brothers were first detained in Romania in December 2022 over a separate human trafficking investigation, which led to a criminal indictment in 2023 accusing them of running an organized crime operation built around exploiting women. That Romanian case has dragged on for years, with Andrew Tate recently losing an appeal to relax the judicial restrictions he's been living under while the trial continues.

The brothers have denied all wrongdoing throughout, and their attorney told reporters following the Miami arrest that they intend to contest the UK's extradition request. Assistant Chief Constable Karena Thomas of Bedfordshire Police, whose major crime unit led the investigation behind the new charges, said the case reflected close cooperation between national and international law enforcement agencies.
Testing Political Ties

The arrest carries an added layer of intrigue given the Tates' visibility within pro-Trump online circles. Andrew Tate has built a following among prominent voices on the American right, and the brothers were seen attending events alongside senior US officials as recently as this spring. But when the UK's extradition request landed, the Trump administration signaled it would not intervene, with White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt issuing a brief statement in July confirming there were no plans to step in on the brothers' behalf.

That response marked a notable shift for a movement that had previously embraced the Tates as symbols of a broader cultural fight, and it left several of their past political allies conspicuously quiet. Only a small number of figures, including Rep. Abe Hamadeh of Arizona, publicly pushed back against the extradition effort.

The brothers are scheduled to continue fighting the extradition request in Florida federal court, a process that legal experts say could stretch on for months. For now, they remain in custody as both the US and UK legal systems work through one of the more closely watched extradition battles in recent memory.

title: Colombia's Earthquake Death Toll Passes 265 as Rescue Crews Race Against Time
excerpt: The strongest earthquake to hit Colombia this century has killed more than 265 people and left thousands more injured or missing, testing a brand-new government just days into office.
body: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake that tore through western Colombia on Monday has become the deadliest the country has seen this century, with the death toll climbing past 265 as rescue crews continue digging through collapsed buildings four days later. More than 3,700 people have been injured and over 4,100 remain reported missing, according to figures compiled by Colombian authorities and tracked through the week.

The quake struck near San José del Palmar in the department of Chocó, an underdeveloped stretch of western Colombia roughly 150 miles from Bogotá, at a depth of about 103 kilometers. Tremors were felt as far away as neighboring Ecuador and Panama, but the worst destruction hit Cali, Pereira, Quibdó and Manizales, where entire blocks of buildings pancaked to the ground within seconds.
A New President's Baptism by Fire

The disaster landed just days after Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in as Colombia's president, forcing him to lead national emergency response efforts before completing his first week in office.
